source_quote: We developed a “pre-post intervention” study through statistical comparison of HH performance at baseline and the two intervention phases.

value: Phase 1 (January–December 2010, WHO multimodal): leadership/institutional safety climate; alcohol-based hand rub at point of care; education/training; reminders/posters; audit and feedback
source_quote: included the five progressive steps such as administrative support and multidisciplinary approach, promotion of easy access to alcohol hand-rub solutions in points of care (AHR at bedside) educational interventions, strategically placed reminders, audits by direct observation and feedback on performance.
location: Discussion, Comparison with other studies (also Table 1)

value: Phase 2 (January–December 2011, added to phase 1): alcohol-based hand rub at point of care (extended to all beds); audit and feedback (audits 3 days every 3 weeks, bimonthly control-chart feedback); other (standardized proactive corrective actions; Statistical Process Control charts)
source_quote: The main interventions added during phase II as regards phase I (table 1) were: a) increase of AHR dispensers placement (from 0.57 dispensers/bed to 1.56); b) increase of frequency audits (from 25 days to 51 days and audits were dispersed more evenly over time [2 vs 17 evaluation periods]); c) feedback was more standardized and statistical control graphs were shown to health care workers in a bimonthly fashion; and d) implementation of a standardized process for proactive corrective actions.
